issues.description: The problem statement requires the Book struct to have a property named `title` (and `author`) and an optional `genres` array. In the provided solution the Book struct declares the title property as `bookTitle` while the Client code and Book initializers use `title` (e.g. Book(title: ...), book.title). This name mismatch between the Book struct and its usage contradicts the specification and will prevent the code from compiling and confuse students about the expected property names.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Book struct with the problem specification by renaming the `bookTitle` property to `title` (let title: String). Ensure the Book struct's property names match the memberwise initializer labels and all usages in Client (Book(title: ...), book.title). Alternatively, update the Client and problem statement to consistently use `bookTitle`, but the preferred fix is to follow the problem statement and use `title`.

issues.description: The Book's title property is named inconsistently: the problem statement (and the Client implementation) refer to the property as 'title', but the Book struct in the solution defines the property as 'bookTitle'. This mismatch makes it unclear which identifier students should implement and leads to client code referencing a non-existent member.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Book struct use the property name 'title' to match the problem statement and client usage (rename 'bookTitle' to 'title'), or alternatively update the problem text and all client code to use 'bookTitle' consistently. Prefer renaming the struct property to 'title' to minimize student confusion.
